## [#10947: fix: support shift+click range selection on table row checkboxes](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10947)

- **Change:** high complexity: adds shift-click range selection to table selection checkboxes and changes the shared selection manager's fallback anchor, spanning hooks, state and RAC integration tests. Controlled selection supplied as a plain `Set` would use the last selected key when anchor metadata is absent, affecting range selection beyond checkbox clicks.
- **API / compatibility:** no new named prop, export or type, but existing selection behavior changes. The [hook patch, lines 47-66](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/9de0539981216c7e7b170aac7b500ad66e4cd193/packages/react-aria/src/table/useTableSelectionCheckbox.ts#L47-L66) adds `onClickCapture` and overrides `onChange`; [SelectionManager.ts around line 243](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/9de0539981216c7e7b170aac7b500ad66e4cd193/packages/react-stately/src/selection/SelectionManager.ts#L240-L250) changes `selectedKeys.anchorKey ?? mappedToKey` to include `this.lastSelectedKey`. This shared fallback warrants API/interaction review, including whether the new checkbox contract and anchor semantics are intended across consumers. No DOM structure, class, data-attribute or CSS-variable change is present in the patch.
- **Readiness context:** the [description](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10947) clearly explains the problem and supplies a RAC reproduction, but links no issue and says monorepo tests/lint/types were not run locally. It adds two RAC Table interaction tests and reports separate consuming-app tests; neither claim was executed here. Current GitHub checks show failures in lint, test, test-16/17/18, test-build and typecheck-docs, plus the aggregate `commit` check. The GitHub check summary lists failed jobs but no diagnostic annotations, so attribution to this patch is unverified. CLA is `ACTION_REQUIRED`.
- **Duplicates / direction:** searches for shift/checkbox, table shift selection, checkbox range selection, `extendSelection` and `useTableSelectionCheckbox` found no supported competing PR or issue. No duplicate notice or closure is proposed. A maintainer still needs to establish direction for the feature and shared anchor change; an understandable reproduction is not evidence that the team has agreed to those semantics. Medium/high scope review only, not a full low-complexity red-flag review.
- **Labels (proposed):** add `merge-risk: high` for cross-layer shared selection behavior and unresolved CI failures; `ai-reviewed` for completed bounded read-only triage; `needs API review` for the changed interaction/anchor contract; `needs decision` to decide whether checkbox shift-range selection and the shared fallback are the desired semantics; `waiting for author` to investigate the failing jobs and provide results or evidence they are unrelated. Remove none. All exist except exact `waiting for author`; do not substitute `waiting on author` or create a label.
- **Maintainer next step:** not ready. Establish scope and API direction, then ask for CI failure diagnosis and reproducible verification of the agreed behavior. CLA also blocks readiness but is handled separately, not the reason for the waiting label. Confidence in CI attribution is low because only the job-level failure summary is available; do not describe the failures as proven patch defects.

**Would have done**

- **Labels / readiness:** propose the five additions above, exactly one merge-risk label, no removals and no `ready for review` recommendation yet.
- **Comment / close:** none; no supported duplicate.
- **Other:** retain the feature decision and CI investigation as maintainer actions. No comment, assignment, review or other GitHub write.

## [#10945: fix(Button): remove the pending announcement when the button unmounts](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10945)

- **Change:** high complexity: makes live announcements individually removable and cleans up a focused Button's pending announcement when it unmounts or announces a newer state. This crosses the shared announcer hook layer and RAC Button, changing the lifetime of screen-reader announcements rather than merely silencing an audit result.
- **API / compatibility:** [LiveAnnouncer.tsx, lines 24-64](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/77c43641d0702eec44eda6718d21a4d39d5af9ab/packages/react-aria/src/live-announcer/LiveAnnouncer.tsx#L24-L64) changes exported `announce(...): void` to `announce(...): () => void`, including cancellation of deferred insertion. Main's `packages/@react-aria/live-announcer/src/index.ts` publicly re-exports `announce`, so this is a public return-type addition, not just an internal Button refactor. Existing callers can ignore the return, but observable return values/types change. [Button.tsx, lines 148-163](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/77c43641d0702eec44eda6718d21a4d39d5af9ab/packages/react-aria-components/src/Button.tsx#L148-L163) replaces previous announcements and removes the latest on unmount; ephemeral live-region DOM changes, with no changed consumer prop, class, data-attribute name or CSS variable.
- **Unresolved direction / accessibility:** related [#10579](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10579) remains closed. [snowystinger explicitly requested real-device testing to determine whether removal cuts off speech](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10579#issuecomment-5562788921). A later [VoiceOver report](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10579#issuecomment-6624443450) demonstrates stale navigation, but the [latest maintainer reply](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10579#issuecomment-6630846723) still asks whether this happens to humans in a real application before reopening. The PR says it has not measured whether removal cuts off speech. These are unresolved user-impact and speech-lifetime questions, not evidence that the team has accepted this fix.
- **Readiness context:** two Button tests exercise rendered announcement cleanup and replacement; no new announcer-specific cancellation test is included. The description provides commands and results, but reports four local DatePicker/DateRangePicker failures as also occurring on main; that attribution was not executed or independently established. Current returned CI passes apart from CLA `ACTION_REQUIRED`. The human-understanding checklist is unchecked, but the description says the work was reviewed; an unchecked box alone is not evidence of incomplete understanding.
- **Duplicates:** searches for #10579, pending announcements, `LiveAnnouncer`, live-announcer unmounts and dangling labelled-by references found no supported competing fix. The closed issue is the originating report, not a duplicate PR to close. Medium/high scope review only, not a full low-complexity red-flag review.
- **Labels (proposed):** add `merge-risk: high` for shared screen-reader announcement lifetime and unverified speech interruption; `ai-reviewed` for bounded read-only triage; `needs API review` for the public remover return type; `needs decision` for whether the real-application evidence warrants changing announcement lifetime; `waiting for author` for real-device speech-continuity evidence and a response to the outstanding application-context question. Remove none; retain `Button` and `RAC`. All additions exist except exact `waiting for author`.
- **Maintainer next step:** not ready. Have snowystinger reassess the closed issue against the later report and proposed cleanup, obtain real-device results for quick unmount/replacement and speech completion, and review the public remover contract and cancellation coverage. CLA is handled by separate automation and does not motivate a waiting label. Confidence in screen-reader safety is limited by the explicitly missing measurement.

**Would have done**

- **Labels / readiness:** propose the five additions above, exactly one merge-risk label, no removals and no `ready for review` recommendation yet.
- **Comment / close:** none; no supported duplicate or closure recommendation.
- **Other:** record the API decision, missing evidence and unsigned CLA for maintainers. Do not reopen #10579, request changes, assign anyone or post a comment.

## [#10946: fix: don't add a redundant role to Separator's hr](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10946)

- **Change:** low complexity: three added/three removed source lines in one RAC component plus rendered-output tests. Default Separator uses the implicit role of `<hr>`; vertical separators receive the role and orientation appropriate to the actual rendered `<div>`.
- **Issue / agreed approach:** [#10894](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10894) reproduces the redundant attribute with `<Separator />`. Both issue comments were read: [snowystinger suggests defaulting `elementType` in destructuring](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10894#issuecomment-6527590768), and another contributor offers to implement the same default/resolved-element approach, but no competing PR was found. The [source patch, lines 68-80](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/98f7cf8eb69a1818a3113f4201e3b076a5b79be6/packages/react-aria-components/src/Separator.tsx#L68-L80) follows the suggestion and also passes `elementType: Element`, avoiding role loss for `elementType="hr" orientation="vertical"`. No contradictory maintainer instruction was found.
- **Existing solution / main:** `<Separator elementType="hr" />` already avoids the redundant role for a horizontal separator. Main's [useSeparator.ts, lines 47-66](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria/src/separator/useSeparator.ts#L47-L66) omits the explicit role when given `hr`, while [Separator.tsx, lines 68-80](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria-components/src/Separator.tsx#L68-L80) still passes the unresolved prop. The workaround is not a full replacement: the default remains wrong and explicit `hr` with vertical orientation loses its role on main. RSP's existing [Divider.tsx, lines 62-70](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/%40adobe/react-spectrum/src/divider/Divider.tsx#L62-L70) already passes the resolved element. The Separator and useSeparator docs under `packages/dev/s2-docs/pages/react-aria/` expose the component/hook APIs but do not supply a different default-role solution.
- **API / compatibility:** no new or removed prop, export, event or type, and no changed element/tag selection, class, data-attribute or CSS variable. The default horizontal `<hr>` loses its explicit `role="separator"` attribute while retaining implicit semantics; selectors such as `[role="separator"]` no longer match it. Explicit `hr` plus vertical orientation gains `role="separator"` and `aria-orientation="vertical"` on the existing `<div>`. The description acknowledges selector compatibility, so record an intentional DOM-attribute change rather than promising no consumer-visible change.
- **Verification / red flags:** [Separator.test.js, lines 61-90](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/98f7cf8eb69a1818a3113f4201e3b076a5b79be6/packages/react-aria-components/test/Separator.test.js#L61-L90) queries the accessible role and checks actual tags/attributes for default, horizontal div and three vertical variants. Reasoning from main, the default-role and vertical-explicit-hr cases fail before the patch; these are integration-level assertions for the reported DOM reproduction. The author supplies standalone test instructions and reports red/green results; current returned CI and CLA pass. No added check suppression, type escape, timing hack, DOM poking, user-agent sniffing or removed keyboard/focus support appears in the diff. No mandatory security-review trigger files are changed. All verification here was by reading, not running tests or using a screen reader.
- **Duplicates / review status:** searches for #10894, redundant separator roles, Separator and recent `Separator.tsx` mentions found no supported competing fix. A volunteer issue comment alone is not a duplicate submission. reidbarber, a `MEMBER` reviewer, already approved this exact head, `98f7cf8eb69a1818a3113f4201e3b076a5b79be6`, in the PR's returned reviews. That establishes review progress, not the author's membership. REST still reports `mergeable_state: blocked`; this does not establish a code defect or identify an unmet repository requirement.
- **Labels (proposed):** add `small review` for a focused low-complexity component fix; `merge-risk: medium` for the observable role-selector compatibility change; `ai-reviewed` for completed read-only triage; `has workaround` for explicit horizontal `elementType="hr"`; `needs decision` to confirm that the default/vertical fix should proceed despite that partial workaround and that role-selector compatibility is accepted. Remove none; retain `RAC` and `Separator`. All five additions exist. No `regression` proposal because previously working behavior was not established.
- **Maintainer next step:** substantive review has already occurred and no author-side blocker was identified. Confirm the narrow workaround/compatibility decision, likely answerable from the existing approval, and check the repository's remaining merge gate; once confirmed, recommend maintainer-applied `ready for review` for workflow tracking, not a redundant review request. No separate named API expansion is proposed; the DOM compatibility decision is recorded explicitly. Do not recommend closing the fix solely because a partial workaround exists.

**Would have done**

- **Labels / readiness:** propose the five additions above, exactly one merge-risk label and no removals. Recommend `ready for review` only after the recorded compatibility decision is confirmed; do not apply it automatically.
- **Comment / close:** none; no supported duplicate.
- **Other:** retain the existing approval and use the maintainer's workflow for the remaining decision/merge gate. No comment, review, assignment or GitHub edit.
